When the wife of a wealthy local businessman disappears, Barnaby finds that Fawcett Green harbors a complex web of financial and romantic entanglements.

A school teacher Connie Bishop, Nancy Carroll, who is known to sleepwalk, begins to believe that she has slit the throats of her mentor and a local handyman. A film historian writing about a 1960s horror actress is killed in her home. It becomes the start of what appear to be a series of copycat murders based on the actress' films.
The unveiling of a newly-discovered novel by deceased Midsomer crime-writer George Summersbee is jeopardised.
Vandalism and violence send shock waves through Midsomer's cloistered nunnery.
A pub landlady is crushed to death during a magic show in Midsomer Oaks.
The drowning of a woman in a bathtub is the first in a series of copycat murders imitating infamous killings from the past.
Could a ballad made famous by late, lamented folk singer Johnny Carver be an inspiration for murder?
Barnaby investigates the murder of a boy during a traditional annual race at an exclusive private school but is met with resentment.
The fizz goes out of a sparkling wine launch when the glasses are laced with poison.
A group of conservationists objects to the development of a pristine part of the village and adherents from both sides of the disagreement become victims of a mysterious killer.
When a local DJ is crushed to death at a traditional girls boarding school, new DCI John Barnaby soon discovers that murder and deception are never far away.
During a total eclipse of the sun, an astronomer is bludgeoned to death by a meteor, and an astrologer claims to have predicted each subsequent murder.
The reclusive life of elderly eccentrics William and Mary Bingham comes under police scrutiny when a social services investigator is killed. Barnaby and Jones must unearth generations of secrets
The discovery of a body covered in live rabbits reveals a sinister side to the local pet show. Is this a rivalry taken too far or is the killer driven by something darker?
When a young woman is dressed like a bride and drowned in a bath, it triggers a spate of ghoulish wedding-themed murders in Great Worthy. The case takes Barnaby and Jones to a donkey sanctuary.
A gifted young pianist with emotional issues is in competition with other young talents for a scholarship to a prestigious private musical academy.
Jones goes undercover at the Oblong Foundation after one of the cults young female members disappears suddenly. But he and Barnaby soon start digging into an old case.
A troubled schoolteacher, subject to sleepwalking and quasi-paranoia, feels that an intruder has been in her house, and doubters find dead bodies to confirm her fears.
Fingers point at local druids when a farmer is found horribly murdered at a sacred stone circle in Midsomer Mow. But Barnaby is convinced that basic human greed is the real motive for murder.
At the factory where the world-famous Midsomer Blue Cheese is made, a dairy worker is brutally murdered by a giant round of weaponized cheese.
When a missing tax inspector turns up dead in a vat of cider, Barnaby and Jones must hunt for a giant killer within a Midsomer village steeped in bizarre local traditions.
When a survivalist is found murdered in his bombproof shelter, Barnaby unravels a dark conspiracy.
The cloistered world of Midsomer Priory is forced to open its doors to 21st century policing when a nun is strangled to death.
Something fishy is going on concerning the clubbing deaths of two local residents.
A row between keen birdwatchers in Midsomer-in-the-Marsh turns nasty when their president is killed.
Barnaby gets to relive his former sporting glory when a death at the local Rugby Club sends him and Winter into a muddle of rucks, grudges, romance... and artisanal chocolates?

The villagers of Fletcher's Cross are preparing for their team match against Midsomer Worthy. Tara Cavendish, the second wife of local landowner and cricket captain Robert Cavendish, has since gone missing after taking their dog for a walk.
